argument_summary: The present record supports certification only in a narrowed form: aggregate readiness clears threshold and rehearsal shows no severity-one incidents, so launch readiness is not unsupported in general, but the same admissible record also shows an unresolved below-target clinical-trial intake limitation and an incomplete draft runbook. The supportable position is therefore not clean no-limitations certification. It is certification with explicit limitation disclosure and operational monitoring commitments, which aligns the packet with the evidence already cited.
claims_about_business_cost: No independent business-cost claim is needed to resolve the audit concern. The packet can be aligned to policy by narrowing the certification claim to caveated compliance rather than escalating the matter as if the entire certification basis fails.
claims_about_policy: The policy text does not bar certification in all cases where a limitation remains; it bars certification without material caveats unless the weakness is resolved or covered by an approved mitigation containing the required fields. On this record, draft monitoring artifacts do not remove the disclosure obligation. The compliant reading is that certification can proceed only if treated as caveated compliance tied to disclosure of the clinical-trial intake limitation for the named use case, rather than as a clean certification posture.
concessions: The clinical-trial intake slice remains below target and is concentrated in protocol eligibility support.
The draft mitigation runbook is incomplete because owner and alert threshold are still TBD.
The current model-card draft cannot support a no-known-material-limitations statement on this record.
Draft monitoring and rollback intentions are not equivalent to approved mitigation under the stated policy.
